This play that mentions the stage direction "Exeunt Servants, running about as if frightened, different ways" features a chase through "feather-bed lane" and "up and down hill." Based off of incidents involving Cornelius Kelly as written by Mrs. Hodson, David Garrick wrote the prologue to this play that features Mr. Woodward weeping. One character is given a letter about some fresh horses whose contents are altered to gambling instead, while Sir Charles's son woos what he thinks is a barmaid, in what might be Three Pigeons Bar. Marlow and Kate desire to marry in this play set at Mrs. Hardcastle's home. Constance Neville loves Hastings in, what play featuring Tony Lumpkin written by Oliver Goldsmith?

A speaker praises these objects by saying "We thought they were a windfall," and describing how "your daughter came with her armfuls, eager and happy." Another poem about these entities says they are fleeting "like the summer's rain or as the pearls of morning's dew," and describes how we weep because they "haste away so soon." Those poems are by Ted Hughes and Robert Herrick respectively. Another poem about these entities notes how "they flash upon that inward eye, which is the bliss of solitude," and even though "the waves beside them danced, but they outdid the sparkling waves in glee." These objects are "continuous as the stars that shine...they stretched in a never ending line." while wandering lonely as a cloud, William Wordsworth observed what flower?

In one section of this work, a woman accepts her husband's "story of being kidnapped by pirates on Lake Michigan" to preserve their marriage. One of its sections tells a "joke of cosmic size" from Professor Newcomer. One character in this work asks why everyone lets Dora and Benjamin Pantier's son and his lover make a resting place their "unholy pillow." This book including sections about Sexsmith the Dentist and Abraham Lincoln's supposed lover Ann Rutledge. It opens with a poem about Elmer, Herman, Ella and Kate, all of whom are "sleeping on the hill." identify this book of poetry about some dead Midwesterners, by Edgar Lee Masters.

Hisao reveals to Asako that he plans to assassinate his father in this man's play The Rokumeikan. Akio likens the tears of his former lover to the title objects in "Fountains in the Rain," from his collection Acts of Worship. Noguchi marries the proprietress of the Setsugoan in his After the Banquet. Fusako's fiancé Ryuji is given drugged tea at the end of another of this man's novels, The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea. In one of his works, the line "when you meet the Buddha, kill him" convinces Mizoguchi to burn down the Kinkakuji. Name this author of The Temple of the Golden Pavilion and Confessions of a Mask who killed himself on live TV in Japan.

A discussion and recitation of Pushkin's "The Poor Knight" in this novel annoys a character whose son is offered 75,000 rubles to marry a woman he hates. One character in this work writes an "Essential Statement," and that man, Hippolyte, explains at a party that he will kill himself the next time the sun rises. The main character of this work breaks a vase at a party and rejects Aglaya, who absconds with a man posing as a count. That title character finds Nastasya murdered in the bed of a rival he met on the way home from a Swiss sanatorium, Rogozhin. Name this novel about the foolish Prince Myshkin, by Feodor Dostoyevsky.

The narrator of one of his short stories disapproves of the title character's desire to be a jazz pianist, while Jo commits perjury as Parnell defends the store-owner Lyle in a case concerning Richard's murder in another work. The title character of one of his novel murders Guillaume after ending a homosexual relationship with the protagonist David, and another work features characters such as Florence and Elizabeth Grimes and centers on the stepson of Stephen Gabriel who attains salvation on his fourteenth birthday. Identify this author of "Sonny's Blues," Blues for Mister Charlie, Giovanni's Room, and Go Tell it on the Mountain.

The creator of one of these objects, Heinrich, falls in love with the elfish spirit Rautendelein in a work by Gerhart Hauptmann, while Dora Greenfield and Toby Gashe discover one near the Imber Abbey in a novel by Iris Murdoch. In another novel, Major Joppolo attempts to find one of these objects for the titular Italian town. A poem about these objects describes "what a world of merriment their melody foretells," and they also appear in the title of a work where Robert Jordan attempts to blow up a bridge in Spain. Identify these objects whose "tintinnabulation" is described in an Edgar Allen Poe poem, and which toll in a work by Hemingway.

The speaker of this poem describes experience as "an arch wherethrough gleams / that untraveled world," but earlier notes that "I am become a name." The title character praises his son who can "make mild a rugged people" but laments his duty to "mete and dole unequal laws to a savage race." The title character "cannot rest from travel" but claims "I am a part of all that I have met" after describing the "drunk delight" of battle in Troy. The title figure is determined to "to touch the Happy isles / and see Achilles," and resolves "To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield." identify this poem about an Ithacan king by Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

One author from this country wrote described Andres dreaming about meeting a Cuban, and recounts a kidnapping of the Vip by members of "the Screwery." One of this country's leaders described the life of the titular "Tiger of the Plains" during the rule of Juan Rosas. Another author from here described the adolescent years of the movie crazed Jose Casals, while another wrote about Yu Tsun, who realizes that the title entity is a novel written by Ts'ui Pen. Name this country, home to the authors of Facundo, Betrayed by Rita Hayworth, and "The Garden of Forking Paths," the home country of Manuel Puig and Jorge Luis Borges.

In a work by this man, Prosperine is the secretary of James Morell, and that work sees Eugene Marchbanks declare his love to the title character. His other works include one in which George Crofts and Frank Gardner both want to marry one central character. In another of his works, Raina Petkoff marries her "chocolate cream soldier," Captain Bluntschli. Another work by this playwright of Candida features characters like Colonel Pickering, and centers on Henry Higgins' bet that he can purify Eliza Doolittle's speech. Name this playwright of Arms and the Man, and Mrs. Warren's Profession, Major Barbara, and Pygmalion.

This author wrote about a girl who refuses to throw away a chicken sandwich in "Just Before the War With the Eskimos." Another work by this author features a boy with "rickets in one leg and elephantiasis in other" fishing next to a "No Fishing!" sign while in Montreal. "The Chief" tells members of the "Comanche Club" a story about a deformed criminal named the "Laughing Man" in one of his works. Another work by this man sees the central character chat with Sibyl on the beach before shooting himself in the head. Name this creator of Seymour Glass in "A Perfect Day for Bananafish," who wrote about Holden in The Catcher in the Rye.

One work by this author notes "Surgeons must be very careful/ Where they take their knife!" while another poem declares that "You cannot put a fire out." A work by this poet states that "Much sense is the starkest madness," and that "Much madness is divinest sense," and one poem by this poet notes that "Not one of all the purple host" could define victory as well as he who was defeated in "Success is counted sweetest." One of this author's poems compares hope to "the thing with feathers," and about a carriage that contained both her and eternity. Name this poet of "I heard a fly buzz when I died" and "Because I could not stop for death."

Enoch unmasks an elder in one scene in this novel, and one character decides to add a section on the last scene of the book to his own book, titled after "The Pacification of the Primitive Tribes." The protagonist of this work often declares that "when a man says yes, his chi also says yes," and in one scene, he beats his wife during the Week of Peace. One character sacrifices Ikemefuna after treating him well for many years, and other characters in this novel include Nwoye, the protagonist's son, who converts to Christianity. Okonkwo commits suicide after a failed revolt against colonial powers in, which work of Chinua Achebe?

One of this man's novels centers around the Tolm family, which is overwhelmed by the titular phenomenon, while in the title character of another work is a maid who gets mixed up with a case involving Ludwig Gotten, and shoots Werner Totges after he asks "how about a bang?" In addition to The Safety Net and The Lost Honor of Katharina Blum, he described a character who befriends Rahel, falls in love with Boris, and bears the child Lev, while various members of the Faehmel family reconcile in September 1958 as Robert routinely plays the title game in another novel. Identify this author of Group Portrait with Lady and Billiards at Half-Past Nine.

One character traveled to New York with a theatre group performing a play called "Ours Was the Shame", and meets a friend of his brother's while buying medicine for his gonorrhea. A supermarket magnate has been slowly running the village stores out of business in this novel, and the narrator's brother starts a soccer team as a ruse to gather the village's young men to revolt against the "Emperor's" Korean store. Takashi reveals that he had had an affair with his retarded sister before committing suicide in this work. This novel chronicles Mitsu's return to his village home, and it begins with an episode recalling a friend who paints his face red and inserts a cucumber in his anus before hanging himself. Name this novel titled for an unheard plea, by Kenzaburo Oe.

In one early scene in this play, one character suggests that the outside environs are the "ghoul-haunted woodland of Weir" and references Edgar Allan Poe. One of this play's supporting characters works on the precision bench in the spare parts department and is judged to "look superior" compared to the rest of his friends. An unseen character is the "extremely good-looking" poet Allan Grey, who turned out to be a "degenerate" before killing himself. At one point in this play, a character angrily asserts that he is "one hundred percent American" and "not a Polack." This play primarily takes place at Elysian Fields Avenue, where we see such characters as Mitch and Stanley. Identify this work by Tennessee Williams that describes what happens when Blanche DuBois takes the titular conveyance to visit her sister Stella.

The second stanza of this poem describes a woman who spends her days in "ignorant good-will" and her nights in argument. This poem asks questions such as "What is it but nightfall?" "O when may it suffice?" and "Was it needless death after all?" This poem starts off stating that, "I have met them at close of day/ coming with vivid faces," and concludes by saying, "A terrible beauty is born." This poem references people that were involved in the event this poem was based on such as MacDonagh, MacBride, Connolly, and Pearse. Name this poem that describes an important historical event that featured Michael Collins, a William Butler Yeats poem that is titled after the holiday and year of an important day in Irish history.

One incident in this story sees a character recounting a story about a present delivered to Alexander the Great of a living woman, which another character dismisses as "a childish fable." At one point, two characters conspire to use the contents of a Cellini vase upon the titular character in order to thwart someone they call "a vile empiric" and someone "not to be tolerated by those who respect the rules of the medical profession." This story begins when a student named Giovanni arrives at Padua and becomes entranced by his neighbor's garden. Informed by Professor Baglioni of the sinister nature of his neighbor, Giovanni is horrified to see the titular character die after consuming the antidote he gives her. Identify this Nathaniel Hawthorne story about a scientist who experiments on his daughter to make her poisonous to humans.

One of this man's lesser known novels is about a white man who discovers while doing research on his family that he has African-American heritage and thus begins to think of himself as black. Another of this man's novels is about the head of the Revelation Automobile Company, who marries the beautiful socialite Fran Voelker. Yet another novel explores reporter Doremus Jessup who becomes opposed to the political stances of Buzz Windrip. Besides Kingsblood Royal and It Can't Happen Here, this author is better known for tracing the lives of various Midwesterners from the state of Winnemac, many of whom either live in or visit the large city of Zenith, including the titular characters Samuel Dodsworth and Martin Arrowsmith. Identify this American author who satirized small town life with such novels as Main Street and Babbitt.

This man was the first to translate John Barclay's poem Argenis, and the title character of one of his works is revealed to be a man by Dauphine, after Morose marries the title character. This author of Epicene and collaborated with John Marston and George Chapman on Eastward Ho! He also wrote about Littlewit, Winwife, and Dame Purecraft attending the title event, while the title character of another work attempts to convince Corbaccio and Corvino of his impending death. In his best known work, Sir Pertinax Surly sees through the opreations of Doctor Subtle and Face, who dupe people such as Epicure Mammon. Identify this author of Bartholomew Fair, Volpone and The Alchemist.

This man's works were called a "farrago of nonsense" in Bertrand Russell's Unpopular Essays and he posited that free will can only exist within contracts and property rights in another work. He outlined the relationship between of the state and the family and declared that the state is "the presence of God on Earth" in one work, and he divided the mind into the objective, subjective, and absolute in another. In addition to Science of Logic and Elements of the Philosophy of Right, this man wrote a work in which men approach a state of "Absolute Consciousness" and outlined the origins of the master/slave relationship. Best known for formulating the thesis-antithesis-sythesis form of the dialectic, name this German philosopher, author of Phenomenology of Spirit.

One of his works describes the decay of the food-obsessed couple Afansy and Pulcheria after Pulcheria's death, while another of his creations is enraged to see his son join the voivod of Kiev during the siege of Dubno, and witnesses the execution of Ostap. In addition, one of his works sees people such as Manilov and Korbochka sell the title beings to Pavel Chichikov, and in one of his stories, the protagonist visits the "prominent personage" after the title article of clothing is stolen from him. Identify this author of "Old World Landowners," Taras Bulba, and Dead Souls, who wrote about Akaki Akakievich in "The Overcoat."

This author wrote about Gregory Reeves in one novel, another features Pedro de Validivia. In addition to The Infinite Plan and Inés of My Soul, this author wrote about a title character who was conceived when her mother slept with a man on his deathbed due to snakebite. One of this author's novels takes place partially in California, and features Joaquin Andieta and Eliza Sommers, and is titled Daughter of Fortune. She wrote a novel about Riad Halabi and Rolf Carlé titled Eva Luna, but this author's best known novel features an estate called Tres Marias. Name this author who created the Trueba family, a Chilean women best known for House of the Spirits.

This author used Anderson's setting Winesburg, Ohio for a college attended by Marcus Messner in his novel Indignation. One of this author's short stories sees Ozzie Freeman threaten to jump off a roof unless a crowd acknowledges the virgin birth. One of this author's narrators recounts Seymour "Swede" Levov, and this author wrote a work that treats the Monica Lewinsky hearings and features Coleman Silk. This author of American Pastoral and The Human Stain wrote a work in which the title character confesses his deviant sexual behavior to his psychologist. Name this Jewish American author of Portnoy's Complaint.

In a story named for a practitioner of this activity, it is done first at the Westerhazys ', then at a wild party at the Biswangers ', and finally at Bullet Park; that retelling of the myth of Narcissus features Neddy Merrill, and is by John Cheever. Lord Byron declares himself a "degenerate modern wretch" in a poem "Written after" doing this activity. A seven-day-long contest in this activity is undertaken in full armor by Breca and Beowulf. One literary character who does this activity is a youth from Abydos who did it each evening to visit a tower in Sestos. Name this activity that Leander did to visit Hero each night until he died after failing at it.

In this work, one character chafes at having been "scalped," demoted from boss to assistant, and demands a more important role for his son. One character refuses Brovik, but is convinced to let go Brovik's son Ragnor go by a character who demands the "Kingdom" she has been promised, Hilda Wangel. Those demands lead the protagonist of this work to attempt to replicate a ritual he performed at a church dedication in her hometown for his wife Aline, but as he reaches the top of the large tower on the house that he himself created, he falls to his death. Name this play about Halverd Solness, an architect; a work by Henrik Ibsen.

One controversial claim about this work is that its references to Outremer date it to the First Crusade, and the oldest version of this work contains a line about its possible author Turoldus. The title character's father Milon earns the enmity of the king for marrying Princess Bertha. Mandricardo fights the title character to try to complete his set of Hector's armor. A white stag guides this work's title character through the Alps, and he fights many battles with Ogier the Dane. The title character dies while blowing his horn, and wields Durandal. Name this chanson de geste about the title paladin's death in a Saracen ambush in Roncevaux Pass.

In a work whose title begins with this word, the "Individualistic Assumptions" and "Compensation Principle" are theorized. Max Ringlemann's work on the bystander effect led to his theorizes this type of "loafing." In a work that posits "strain theory," Robert K. Merton paired this word with "Theory" and "Structure." This word comes before "Choice and Individual Values" in a work by Kenneth Arrow, and a work that asks if Spencer is dead is titled after the "Structure" of this type of "Action," was written by Talcott Parsons. Name this word, whose namesake "ology" is practiced by Max Weber and Emile Durkheim.

People who disappear in this work include Midas Mulligan, Richard Haley and Ellis Watt. Quentin Daniels eventually joins them when he attempts to discover the secrets of a scientifically impossible motor. Wesley Mouch passes legislation to cripple industrialists such as Dan Conway in this work. Another of its characters, Ragnar Danneskjold, is a ship-plundering pirate. Francisco d'Anconia crashes the copper market when he learns his mines are to be nationalized. It begins with Eddie's revelation to James Taggart that the Rio Norte Line is going under. Name this novel featuring Dagny Taggart, a novel by Ayn Rand that asks "who is John Galt?"

This author wrote a novel whose title character saves Mordecai's sister from drowning, encounters the gambling Gwendolen Harleth, and searches for the family of Mirah Lapidoth. Another of this author's novels sees one character abandon her baby while searching for its father, Captain Donnithorne. One of this author's novels sees a character courted by Phillip Wakem and Stephen Guest named Maggie Tulliver. Another work by this author of Daniel Deronda and Adam Bede sees Reverend Causabon die, leaving his widow Dorothea Brooke to marry Will Ladislaw. Name this author of The Mill on the Floss and Middlemarch.

The epigraph to this work, which describes "morbid systems" arising from the interregnum between old and new, is by Antonio Gramsci. One of this novel's characters sees a picture of herself in a Life coffee-table book, causing her to wonder why Lydia was carrying her books, and that character's husband later builds a water tank and shoots some boars. Its title character takes the keys to a "bakkie", after which he learns to drive from Daniel, who later steals Bamford's gun. It ends with Maureen abandoning her family to run toward a helicopter. Name this novel whose title character is the servant of the Smales family, a work of Nadine Gordimer.

One character in this work smoothly suggests that he form a "triangular friendship" with a married couple. Another character in this work becomes obsessed with the red-headed singer Diana, and it also features an academic busily researching his book on "The Domestic Industries of Brabant." The final scene of this play sees the title character discussing a "deed of spontaneous beauty" before a man dubbed "the one cock in the basket" states that Eilert did not kill himself voluntarily. Featuring such characters as the dull historian George Tesman and the sly Judge Brack, name this play that ends with the title woman shooting herself, by Henrik Ibsen.

One character in this novel, Viktor Sitnikov, appears in the author's first novel, in which he narrates that novel's protagonist's death during an anarchist revolution in Paris. This novel's heroes return from the university to discover Nikolai's affair with his maid, Fenitchka. The central characters are taken into the salon of the rich widow Anna Odintsova, who falls in love with one protagonist, but is rejected. The other protagonist, Arkady Kirsanov, comes to believe that some things are worthwhile after all, and to reject the nihilism of the other, who dies alone. Name this novel about Bazarov, written by Ivan Turgenev.

This character is first mentioned in a series of four letters addressed to a Mrs. Margaret Saville. He is the object of affection for his adopted sister, who was found in an Italian peasant village. At the end of the work he appears in, this character pursues the murderer of his brother William and friend Henry Clerval to the Arctic Circle, where he dies from pneumonia. This character's creation was inspired by both a sight of lightning striking down a tree during his childhood and the alchemical works of Paracelsus and Albertus Magnus. A notable student of Ingolstadt University, name this man who creates a namesake monster in a novel by Mary Shelley.

Czeslaw Milosz has written a poem titled "Against" a poet from this polity, who dedicated "A Threnody" to his sister and wrote "Rock and Hawk" and "Shine, Perishing Republic!" Another poet from this polity wrote a poem that claims "I pledge allegiance to the soil" that contains lines such as "One ecosystem, in diversity, under the sun, with joyful interpenetration for all." In addition to this polity's Robinson Jeffers and Turtle Island author Gary Snyder, a poem set in this polity imagines Garcia Lorca by the watermelons and Walt Whitman eyeing the grocery boys. Name this state, a "Supermarket" in which names a poem by Allen Ginsberg.

The first section after this work's prologue depicts a plane's shadow over a cheering crowd. The myth that this film was edited down from 250 miles of footage was debunked in the Ray Mueller film about its director's "Wonderful, Horrible Life." "We Are the Dawn" plays as this film opens with a rather homoerotic montage of strapping young men washing one another's backs; its closing scene is compiled from footage from an NSDAP rally, much like the director's earlier piece, Der Sieg des Glaubens, which had become unsuitable with the fall from favor of Ernst Röhm. Name this film, a 1935 work of Nazi propagandist Leni Riefenstahl.

A sequel to this work redirects attention to natural beauty and is titled for a certain figure's "garden." It declares that one must rob a baby of its mother's milk in order to drink, and defines joy as "sorrow unmasked." The title figure of this work, which was followed by Sand and Foam, addresses the reader as "a leaf in God's forest" and it includes sections like "Reasons and Passions," and "Eating and Drinking." It begins on the Seventh of Ielool when Almitra begins a discussion in Orphalese as a ship has arrived to return the title figure, al-Mustafa, to the isle of his birth. Name this book by Khalil Gibran.

A one act play by Jonathan Reynolds sees Rupert Murdoch's inability to recite this work launch his career in newspapers. The speaker compares his childhood adventures to a "man flying from something that he dreads," and imagines a hermit "in the houseless woods." The poet recollects the scenery in "'mid the din of towns and cities" and the "heavy burthen" of the "unintelligible world" is lightened at the title locale, whose "green pastoral landscape" has grown "more dear" to the speaker. The speaker recalls a gap of five years after a visit to the title location with sister Dorothy in, what poem about a trip to the River Wye, by William Wordsworth.

This man described a character who has an epitelioma near his mustache, and the Agazzi family watch the conflict between Signora Frolla and Signor Ponza over Signora Ponza's identity in another work. In addition to The Man With the Flower in His Mouth and Right you are! (If you think you are), he wrote about a guy who goes to Monte Carlo and is mistaken for being dead, The Late Mattea Pascal, and a work in which a man who falls off of a horse believes he is the title Holy Roman Emperor. Better known for a work featuring a Boy, Girl, Mother, Father, Stepdaughter, and Son, name this author of Enrico IV and Six Characters in Search of An Author.

The narrator of one poem by this author dismisses a "red sword of virtue," while the speaker of another of his poems from the same collection encounters a "creature, naked, bestial" who "held his heart in his hands/and ate of it." Other works by this author of the collection The Black Riders include a short story in which Johnny accuses the Swede of cheating at a card game, and another based on his own experiences after the sinking of the Commodore. This author of "The Blue Hotel" and "The Open Boat" also wrote novels starring a "girl of the streets" and Private Henry Fleming. Identify this author of Maggie and The Red Badge of Courage.

One character with this occupation incinerates several men dressed as orangutans and lights them on fire in a Poe story. A stage character with this occupation is noted for singing the songs "Come Away, Death" and "The Rain it Raineth Every Day." Another character with this occupation concludes a play by laying out the degrees of the lie and marrying Audrey. An unnamed character with this job claims that "truth's a dog must to kennel" and addresses his boss as "nuncle." Trinculo in The Tempest and Feste in Twelfth Night have this occupation, as does Touchstone in As You Like It. Name this occupation held by a character serving King Lear.

In one work of this author, a professor dying of cancer dictates part of a letter to Mr. Vercueil. Another of his works culminates in a plane dropping "words in Spanish" on the main character. In another work, one character denounces the "smelly underwear" of realism, and Elizabeth Costello gives two lectures on animal rights rather than literature. Susan Barton is thrown from a boat on route to Lisbon in his retelling of Robinson Crusoe titled Foe, and the professor David Lurie seduces one of his students in Disgrace. Name this author who wrote of a gardener's trek through Apartheid era South Africa in his Life & Times of Michael K.

One of this man's poems ends with a question regarding a boat disappearing on the "black waters of the Lethe." Another of his works ends with the comment that he is putting his "queer shoulder to the wheel," and he updated William Blake in a poem inspired that claims the title flower is not a train. This author of "America" and "Sunflower Sutra," addressed another poem to Carl Solomon that contains the refrain "I'm with you in Rockland" and whose second section describes the nightmare Moloch. Name this American poet who wrote about seeing "the best minds of my generation destroyed" in the long poem Howl.

One author from this country wrote about Adah, who leaves Pussy Cat Mansions. Another author from this country wrote a novel "in Rotten English." In addition to the authors of In the Ditch and Sozaboy, another author from this country wrote the poems "Elegy For Alto" and "Heavensgate." Those authors from this country are Buchi Emecheta, Ken Saro-Wiwa, and Christopher Okigbo. Another author from this country wrote novels like A Man of the People and Anthills of the Savannah. Name this country, home to the author of Arrow of God, Chinua Achebe.

One character in this novel dies under unexplained circumstances after he takes out a large insurance policy in his lover's name. One character's lover has an affair with Sir Pitt, her husband's brother, while he is in jail for gambling debts in this work. In addition to the protagonist's failed marriage with Rawdon Crawley, this novel sees its protagonist meet her best friend at Miss Pinkerton's School, and another character marries George Osborne, although she was loved by Captain Dobbin. Name this novel about Amelia Sedley and Becky Sharp, a work by William Makepeace Thackeray.

Minor characters in this work include Samson and Armistid, who serve as hosts for the main characters during their journey. Other characters in this work include Skeet MacGowan, who works in a drugstore, and Mr. Moseley, a smug druggist in Mottson. One chapter in this work is narrated by the Reverend Whitfield, who had an illegitimate affair with one of the characters, which produced the son Jewel. Noted for the line "My mother is a fish" said by the child Vardaman, this work also features Cash and Dewey Dell. Name this novel by William Faulkner, which describes the attempts of the Bundren family to bury their recently deceased matriarch.

In one of this man's novels, the main character nearly crashes into two Jehovah's Witnesses after running over a dog. One of his non-fictional works contrasts Venezuela's war for independence with an aging conquistador's search, his The Loss of El Dorado. Another of his works features Mr. Popo and the poet B. Wordsworth, who never complete any of their projects. Another of his novels sees the "big man" spell trouble for Salim's new shop. The title character of another of his works must put up with his overzealous Tulsi family he marries into. For 10 poitns, name this Trinidadian author of A Bend in the River and A House for Mr. Biswas.

One character in this work states that female devils have clefts and cloven feet, while the males have horns. Another character in this work heats congealed blood over a fire, and the words "Homo fuge" are inscribed on the arm of the title character, who knows not where he should fly. That title character calls his servants, Valdes and Cornelius, to bring him books on necromancy. After he has the books, his first act of magic is to summon a devil, who will become his servant for the next twenty-four years. Name this play in which the title character summons Mephastophilis and sells his soul to the devil, a work by Christopher Marlowe.

One of this author's works sees Captain Bartlett learn that he had killed a man to protect a buried treasure that turns out to be a chest of worthless trinkets. In another work, this author described a man who recites Baudelaire to a prostitute named Fat Violet. This author of Gold wrote of a man who encounters the "little formless fears," a railway car porter who becomes a dictator sought by Smithers and Lem. He also wrote of Mary's descent into morphine addiction, and of the patrons of Harry Hope's bar who deal with their "pipe dreams." name this author of The Emperor Jones, Long Day's Journey into Night, and The Iceman Cometh.

This author wrote a work in which the fascist Mother Peep gives a speech as Edouard and the main character frantically search for a briefcase containing "evidence" about the title character, who lures victims like Dany to a pool by offering to show them a "picture of the Colonel." Another of his plays sees The Martins pay a visit to The Smiths, and the Fire Chief plays a game of ding-dong ditch and remarks about the titular unseen character "who always wears her hair in the same way". Name this absurdist playwright of The Killer and The Bald Soprano, who also wrote a work in which everyone but Berengér become the titular animals, Rhinoceros.

In this work, the head of one character is buried by hand, and its location is later decorated with marble. That character was killed following the discovery of one of his previous affairs by his future father-in-law, the Marquis de la Mole, who promised him a title and money after his daughter was impregnated. Its protagonist, who was actually in love with his previous lover, Madame de Renal, met Mathilde after a stint in the seminary, as he believed that the church was a more useful tool for attaining power than the army. Name this novel about Julien Sorel, a work by Stendahl in which the church and army are represented by the titular colors.

This is the last name of an author who wrote about an illegitimate daughter of Thomas Jefferson titled Clotel, and another author with this surname described a sleepwalking figure who studies the murder of Waldagrave in Arthur Mervyn and also wrote Wieland. A play by Eugene O'Neill featuring various mask-wearers has a title character by this name, who is called a "Great God." A priest with this last name features in detective stories written by G. K. Chesterton, and it is the last name of a character who sees his wife Faith attend a meeting of devil worshippers. Identify this name of a "Young Goodman" in a Nathaniel Hawthorne short story.

In this work, Mr. Dumby agrees with Lady Statfield that it has been a "quite delightful" season, only to immediately agree that the season was instead "dreadfully dull." It opens as the main character is arranging a fresh bowl of roses, and later the Duchess of Berwick drives the protagonist to rip open a sealed checkbook, finding several large sums given to another woman. That protagonist of this work leaves a letter for her husband and leaves to escape with Lord Darlington, but Ms. Erlynne reveals herself to be Margaret's long lost mother. Name this play by Oscar Wilde, whose title object is Margaret's birthday gift from her husband.

One work of this man features a ritual "to make a mother rip her son like bread/across a banqueting board!" in his adaptation The Bacchae. One of this man's plays contains four alternate endings, and a prostitute called "Madame Tortoise," who is a story-telling spirit. In addition to A Dance of the Forests, he wrote about the teacher Eman who takes the place of a young boy in a ritual in his The Strong Breed, and another work in which Elisen is slighted by Simon Pilkings. One of his works sees Baroka and Lakunle vie for the love of Sidi. Identify this Nigerian playwright best remembered for The Lion and the Jewel and Death and the King's Horseman.

He claimed that "kindness and goodness do not make a fellow tall" in "Lily has a Rose," and retold the story of Little Eva and Eliza in his ballet Tom. He wrote of males who "cannot chat of this and that" in "the boys i mean are not refined." He told of a man "more blond than you" who "will not kiss your... Flag" in his "I Sing of Olaf, Glad and Big." He wrote of "someones marrying their everyones/ laughing their cryings" in one work, and told of a French concentration camp run by Appolyon in World War I in a work based on Pilgrim's Progress. Name this author of "Anyone Lived in a Pretty How Town" and The Enormous Room.

One character in this work has the unladylike habit of going to the post office in inclement weather. One scene in this novel sees the central characters journey to Box Hill, and one character in this novel mortifies the protagonist when she compares the estate of Maple Grove to Hartfield. The protagonist's oft-sick father is fond of calling married characters "poor." One character in this work marries Robert Martin after failing to snag Mr. Elton, and Jane Fairfax, is secretly married to Frank Churchill in this work. This novel ends with the title character married to Mr. Knightley. Name this novel featuring a certain Miss Woodhouse, by Jane Austen.

In one of this author's works, a young woman becomes jealous of a young black girl named Nancy, while another work describes the life of Quebec resident Cecile Auclair. Besides Sapphira and the Slave Girl and Shadows on the Rock, this author wrote of the lives of scholar Godfrey St. Peter and engineer Bartley Alexander in The Professor's House and Alexander's Bridge. She is better known for a work focusing on Jean Marie Latour's religious activities in New Mexico and another work focusing on Alexandra Bergson. Identify this American author who described western expansion in the novels Death Comes for the Archbishop and O Pioneers!

In one play featuring this character, he is first seen naming the "Five Moods" under the tutelage of Mentor Graham. In a poem about this character, "the sins of all the war-lords" burn his heart. He was the subject of a Richard Hofstadter essay that described the "self-made myth." This subject of a play by Robert Sherwood and a poem by Vachel Lindsay that sees him "walk at midnight," was also the subject of a six-volume biography covering his "Prairie Years" and his "War Years" by Carl Sandburg. Name this literary character who is the implied subject of the Walt Whitman poem "O Captain, My Captain!," the sixteenth President of the United States.

One of this man's works discusses the creation of a giant "prostitute spider." In one of this man's works, he describes his country's fascination with toilets, and claims that the western world is "white," in contrast with the title shade of his country. Joji Kawai has an affair with the title waitress in another of his novels. This author of "The Tattooer," "In Praise of Shadows," and Naomi wrote a novel in which the protagonist's wife "goes to Suma" to see her lover Mr. Aso, and another in which Yukiko has a blemish under her eye and Taeko falls ill. Name this Japanese author of Some Prefer Nettles and The Makioka Sisters.

One of this author's novels sees a title character try to wear a pom-pom around his neck in order to hide his giant adam's apple. Nine cooks serve the nameless narrator of one of this man's novels, who is married to Ilsebill. Eddi Amsel and Harry Liebenau narrate sections of this man's work that concentrates on the animal breeding of the Matern family, and this author discussed journalist Paul Pokriefke's reactions to the sinking of the Wilhelm Gustave in another work. This man wrote Crabwalk, Dog Years, Cat and Mouse, and The Flounder. Name this author of the Danzig Trilogy, which contains a novel about Oskar Matzerath, The Tin Drum.

A short story by this author sees Travis take Eckles on a hunting expedition. One of this author's novels sees Mrs. Bowles and Mrs. Phelps break down after reading "Dover Beach." This author wrote about Leo, whose attempts to build a happiness machine go awry when it burns his garage down. In another of this man's novels, the protagonist is married to Mildred, and falls in with Granger after meeting Clarisse McClellan and Faber and surviving a procaine injection from a mechanical hound. Name this author of "A Sound of Thunder" and Dandelion Wine, who wrote about firefighter Guy Montag in Fahrenheit 451.

One character in this work owns a fan made from banana leaves, which can create giant whirlwinds, but she refuses to surrender it to the protagonist until one of the protagonists transforms into a fly and causes her great abdominal pains. One figure in this work was formerly known as the "Golden Cicada" and assembles a team of companions with the help of Guan Yin. Another character in this work has a staff that can shrink to the size of a needle, as well as a suit of golden armor given to him by the dragon king. That protagonist also ate the peaches of immortality while in heaven. Name this work in which Xuanzang goes to India to bring back sutras with the help of Sun Wukong the monkey god, one of the great Chinese classics.

The sacred Jonglingkong lake is found on a mountain named for this thing. The conch shell used as a weapon by the goddess Durga is said to represent this utterance. This utterance is said to cause the three wonders of creation, sustenance, and dissolution. Also known as the pranava, this utterance is traditionally divided into three parts, which might represent the Trimurti or the three oldest Vedas, or alternatively it is said to contain all other sounds, even though post-Sanskrit sound changes have reduced it to two phonemes. Name or make this sound made by Hindus and Buddhists during meditation.

This text describes a war of four kings against five and the conception and birth of a figure who is prophesized to be a "wild donkey of a man". One figure in this text sends a messenger to Nahor's house in order to find a daughter-in-law, and later marries Keturah. Abimelech, the King of Gerar, is struck barren in this text after confusing another figure's wife for his sister. This book describes how the Land of Shinar was home to a notable edifice, while another location in this book is sealed with a flaming sword after a figure created from a rib eats from the tree of knowledge. Name this first book of the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament.

At the beginning of this work, Kilyddid marries Goleuddydd, however, when she becomes pregnant with his heir, she goes insane, and wanders around the countryside until she eventually gives birth with the help of a swineherd. Such is the birth of one major figure in this work, who later becomes infatuated with a woman he has never seen and travels to Celliwig to ask his cousin for help, after which Twrch Tryth the boar is hunted and slain. One figure in this story is the daughter of the giant Ysbaddaden, while another is the cousin of King Arthur. Name this Welsh epic whose name is also the name of its two major characters.

This man compared the impressions and opinions of the mind to the rays of light on a dish of water. He distinguished the "protreptic" and "elenctic" modes amongst the three modes of philosophical discussion. He claimed that "Conduct me, Zeus, and thou o Destiny the way that I am bid by you to go" is amongst the maxims one must always keep at hand. He also argued that one must always behave as at a dinner party, and that a father who runs away to weep when his child is ill behaves less naturally than a man who stays by his child's bedside. He used Aristotle's term prohairesis to refer to volition and the capacity for choice and asked "Must I then die lamenting?" to which he responded "I must be put in chains." He claimed "some things are in our control and some are not" at the beginning of one work, compiled by his student Arrian. Name this former slave and Stoic, whose sayings were collected in his Enchiridion and Discourses.

This work claims "Life is a pure flame, and we live by an invisible sun within us." It argues that we cannot "extenuate the valour of ancient martyrs" because they "parted with life when it was scarce worth living" and that "to subsist in lasting Monuments" was part of the Christian Elysium, but that "all this is nothing in the Metaphysicks of true belief." The "iniquity of oblivion" is illustrated by the fact "Herostratus lives that burnt the temple of Diana; he is almost lost that built it." It claims "what song the Syrens sang, or what name Achilles assumed" are puzzling, though not beyond conjecture. This work's sequel espouses a "higher geometry of nature" via the quincunx, the figure x, and the lozenge shape; that sequel is The Garden of Cyrus. Exemplifying Baroque prose in lines like "man is a noble animal, splendid in ashes, pompous in the grave", name this work of Thomas Browne inspired by the discovery of a Bronze Age funerary site.

This man argued that if one believes a sign s is a reference to an object O, "the causal flummery is otiose" and that he could "easily conceive of it as a possibility" that Caesar was a robot in his "Replies", collected in Perception and Identity. This man's Metaphysics and Common Sense continued the thread of his article ""Has Austin Refuted the Sense-Data Theory?", which was a response to critiques of an earlier work. An amusing Hilary Spurling essay compares this man to Mike Tyson, whom he once stopped from harassing Naomi Campbell at a party. This man's most famous work considers the equivalence of two sentences about the author of Waverley being Scotch in its section on "The Nature of Philosophical Analysis", as well as claiming that "the ethical word is purely emotive." That work opens with a section on "The Elimination of Metaphysics" and advocates the verification principle. Name this philosopher, the author of Language, Truth, and Logic.

One character in this text recommends cutting the ground in the shape of an inverted gamma. In a chapter of The History of Sexuality, Michel Foucault explored the ideology of power inherent in this text's introduction of Ischomachus as a figure skilled in the art of training his wife to perform household chores. The main speaker of this work claims that he is wealthy because his modest property meets all of his needs, and that those with cows are wealthier than those with money. The opening line of this work sees Critobulus affirm that the titular concept is, like medicine or carpentry, the name of a particular kind of knowledge or science. Name this Socratic dialogue by Xenophon about how to run a farm, whose title was adopted as the name of a branch of social science that studies markets.

This work recommends that elders past the age of reproduction should live in poverty and have their wills executed early to improve the standard of living for younger generations, and this work formulates an early theory of government healthcare by calling on monarchs to provide support for pregnant women, elders, and orphans. This work includes a detailed discussion of how to employ courtesans in war and enumerates a "six-fold policy" of diplomacy which consists of strategies derived from the basic pair of sandhi and vigraha, or peace and war. The author also urges monarchs to preserve the caste system and emphasizes that a successful army must include Vaishyas and Shudras. Written under the pen-name Kautilya, FTP, name this Mauryan era text attributed to Chanakya.

One character in this work suggests shaking down two foreigners, Simmias and Cebes, for money. One implicit voice in this work hums "the sound of the flute in the ears of the mystic" in the ears of another character in this work and leads him to "follow the intimations" of his morality. This work argues that one agrees to obey all the laws of a country tacitly by virtue of remaining there after attaining majority. The title character of this dialogue attempts to persuade Socrates by asking him to think of his responsibilities as a father, which Socrates refuses to do; further, he states that the moral views of the common man are worthless in this dialogue. Name this Platonic dialogue which concerns the concepts of justice and what is allowable in cases of injustice, named after a wealthy friend who offers to bust Socrates out of jail.

One of this writer's works contains a section that discusses "The Dark Shadow" and contains antoher section which envisions three companions for a Roman childbirth goddess, Levana. Another work by this writer discusses the Porter scene of a notable play and discusses how psychological response is a method of literary criticism. In addition to Suspiria de Profundis and On the Knocking at the Gate in MacBeth, one of this writer's works contains an autobiographical second section which recounts a near-accident, while the fist section is entitled "The Glory of Motion" and compares a postal worker to a crocodile. In addition to The English Mail-Carriage, this writer's most famous work is divided into the pleasures and pains of the title substance, the latter of which were described asinsomnia, nightmares, frightening visions, and difficult physical symptoms. Identify this notable essayist who wrote Confessions of an English Opium Eater.

This poet wrote a sonnet which includes an allusion to a ninth wave that fills all the soul with its tide to a man that he addressed as "O sightless bard, England's Mæonides!", "Milton," while he wrote about a poet "whose name was writ in water" in his poem addressed to "Keats." He instructs the listener to "tell him not that life is but a mournful dream" in another poem, which also notes that "Art is long, and Time is fleeting." This author of "A Psalm of Life" also created a poem which exhorts Christ to "save us all from a death like this/On the reef of Norman's Woe!" where the title ship wrecked. This author of "The Wreck of the Hesperus" also wrote a long poem in which Gabriel Lajeunesse is the lost lover of the title Arcadian girl. Identify this author of "Evangeline," a Fireside Poet who also wrote The Song of Hiawatha.

One of this author's novels centers around an engineering student who is reading a book called The New Life, which shares its title with that book. In another work by this author, the lawyer Galip finds that his wife Rüya is missing, leading him to search for her. In addition to writing The Black Book, this author wrote about Hoja, a scholar who owns an Italian scholar as a slave and takes him to visit the Sultan in The White Castle, and about the miniaturist Kara in his work My Name is Red. In this author's most famous work, the narrator foreshadows the death of the high school student Necip, and Muhtar marries and divorces Ipek, who is beloved by the poet Ka. Name this author of Snow, a Turkish novelist.

The speaker of this poem wears elaborate disguises like "Rat's coat, crowskin, crossed staves" and "Behaves as the wind behaves." Later, he notes "There are no eyes here, In this valley of dying stars, in this broken jaw of our lost kingdoms." The last section of this poem declares that "between the conception and the creation," and "between the emotion and the response" lies the Shadow, which appears after children "go round the prickly pear at five o'clock in the morning." The last lines of this poem repeat "This is the way the world ends" three times, ending "not with a bang, but a whimper." The epigraph to this poem references Heart of Darkness by declaring "Mistah Kurtz-- he dead," while the first stanza of this poem calls the title characters "stuffed men, leaning together, heads filled with straw." identify this work by T. S. Eliot.

One character in this work battles with the title character for two days and reveals that he's vulnerable in his navel after sleeping on a rock as a pillow. That same character was earlier confronted by the ghost of Argalia, who gives him a magic helmet. That character is Farau, but Bradamante is a female warrior in this work who possesses a magical lance that unseats everyone. Agramante and his allies are the main antagonists in this work, and the English Knight Astolfo flies on a hippogriff to Ethiopia and then to the moon to help cure the title character. Matteo Maria Boiardo wrote the work which this long poem attempts to continue, which told of its title character in love. Name this work which focuses on the titular paladin in the service of Charlemagne, an epic poem by Ludovico Ariosto.

One character in an early novel by this author has the dream of chronicling the entire colonial history of his home nation, but can't due to money; that character is Felipe Montero, who appears in this author's novel Aura. This author overdubbed lines from Jules Supervielle's poem "La Chambre Voisine" on another of his novels, which was dedicated to this author's friend Luis Bunuel and entited Distant Relations. In a better-known novel by this man, which is divided into "The Old World," "The New World," and "The Next World," El Señor attempts to freeze Hispanic tradition but fails. This author of Terra Nostra may be better-known for writing a novel which focuses on a fictional Ambrose Bierce, or one in which Lorenzo is the son of the titular dying tyrannical family head. Name this Mexican author of The Old Gringo and The Death of Artemio Cruz.

Miles, Dean, Serge and Leonard are four people in this novel who comprise a band called the Paranoids. One character in this novel is a former Buchenwald doctor and take joy in prescribing LSD to housewives to solve their problems. In addition, another character in this novel is a Yoyodyne employee who tells the central character about the Peter Penguid society. The central character of this novel is seduced by a man in a hotel room with whom she watches old movies, but he gets tired of trying to remove her multiple layers of clothes. That character, Metzger, is in conflict with a guilt-wracked used car salesman who's married to the central character, Mucho. The title of this novel refers to the auctioning off of a horn stamp used by the Tristero organization to send mail. Identify this novel about the quest to execute the estate of Pierce Inverarity by Oedipa Maas, a shorter novel by Thomas Pynchon.

In one of this author's short stories, one character remarks of the title character "the whole countryside seemed to flow into her eyes;" no person can enjoy having sex with the title character, but everyone wants to do something fine for her, and she sings like a Jewish cantor with a broken voice. In addition to "Fern," this author's most famous work includes a story in which Tom Burwell and Bob Stone are a black and white man who love the woman Lousia. In addition to that story, "Blood Burning Moon," this author wrote The Blue Meridian, but his most famous work also includes a story about a woman whose soul follows her around the city, "Calling Jesus," and one about a beautiful young woman in Georgia, "Karintha." identify this author of the experimental novel Cane, an African-American Quaker.

The protagonist of this novel has to leave his job after vomiting in front of his classroom, which makes him believe that he will certainly be fired. Two characters in this novel discuss their plans to leave everything behind, but only one of them does so; the other is forced to stay in Japan and work as a tour guide. The protagonist of this novel gets married, he drops out of graduate school to do nothing but drink for days on end. During that time, he meets up with a woman who broods over her husband's suicide and does nothing but drink and drunkenly drive her sportscar around Tokyo at night; that woman is his ex-girlfriend Himiko. The protagonist is especially depressed when, after his son Kikuhiko is born, he's diagnosed with a brain hernia. Name this novel about Bird, a work by Kenzaburo Oe.

In one short story by this author, a man decides to provide a sex education for his son by having him observe a newly married couple and a third man through a bulkhead peep hole. In addition to "At Sea," this author wrote about Skvortsov, who was forced to chop wood by Lushkov, but refuses. This author of "The Beggar" wrote another short story in which Kuznichov and Egorushka attempt to cross the titular part of Russia, "The Steppe," and one in which Yakov Ivanov is an undertaker who enjoys playing the titular "Rothschild's Fiddle." Aliokhin and Burkin are wholly unsatisfied with Ivan's tale in a notable short story by this man, who also wrote one about Dmitri Dmitritch Gurov, who takes notice of a new arrival carrying a Pomeranian. Name this author of "Gooseberries" and "The Lady with the Lapdog."

One scene in this work shows a character explaining the purposes of galoshes to another character. One character in this story has to spend a considerably amount of time choosing between reciting a quotation from Shakespeare or one from Browning. After noticing that a petticoat string is trailing down to the floor, the protagonist of this short story reflects on the fact that Patrick is a shade. At a dinner party in this short story, Bartell D'arcy sings "The Lass of Aughrim" with accompaniment from Miss O'Callaghan. That dinner party is held at the house of Julia and Kate, who are the the protagonist's Aunts. This story ends with a paragraph that notes that "The time had come for him to set out on his journey westward" and that snow was "General all over Ireland." identify this story about Greta's love for the deceased Michael Furey and the jealousy that that produces in Gabriel Conroy, the last story in James Joyce's Dubliners.

Along with Mark Costello, this man wrote a structuralist critique of urban music in his work Signifying Rap:Rap and Race in the Urban Present. Under the pseudonym Elizabeth Klemm, this man published a short story entitled "Mister Squishy," which would later reappear along with "The Suffering Channel" in his collection Oblivion: Stories. He wrote a novel in which the protagonist's pet cockatiel becomes extraordinarily vocal, leading to her existential crisis. That novel, written about Lenore Breadsman, is called The Broom of the System. He may be more famous for writing a long novel in which Orin is the punter for the Arizona Cardinals and is the older brother of the protagonist, Hal Incandenza. The author of the essay collection Brief Interviews with Hideous Men, identify this prolific postmodern American novelist best known for writing Infinite Jest.

Daan and Melton fight on their way to a resort where Daan works as a gardener and encounter the snake-charmer PAulus in one play by this author, entitled Marigolds in August. In another play written by this author, Robert shows up at the photography studio of Styles, entitled Sizwe Banzi is Dead. One character in another of this man's plays was evicted from his tenant farm; that man is Boseman, who is walking to another town with Lena. In a better-known play, Sam and Willie are practicing their dancing in preparation for a competition, before Hally returns him from school, and in another work, Morris is the fair-skinned brother of the extremely dark Zachariah. Name this man who wrote Blood Knot and MASTER HAROLD…And the Boys, a South African playwright.

One of this poet's works addresses the title character by saying "My tongue had taught thee comfort, touch had quenched thy tears;" that character, a sick child, would eventually be "powerful amidst peers" at the "random grim forge." That poem, "Felix Randal," appeared in the same collection as one that calls the title month "Mary's Month," entitled "May Magnificat." Also the author of "As Kingfishers Catch Fire," another poem asks why the title concept would "lay a lionlimb against me?" and or scan "With darksome devouring eyes my bruisèd bones?" The title concept of a further poem "over the bent World broods with warm breast and with ah! Bright wings."The author of "Carrion Comfort" and "God's Grandeur," identify this poet who wrote about a "dapple dawn-drawn falcon" in his work "The Windhover,"

This writer collected several of his shorter pieces into the work Fables and Epigrams. In one of this man's works, King Arideus visits the titular prince after he's taken prisoner in his first battle. Hettore Gonzaga gives his chamberlain Marinelli carte blanche to get him a lover affair with the titular character of another of this man's works, Emma Galotti. In one of this man's critical works, he argued against Horace's as painting so poetry stricture; that work is entitled Laocoon: An Essay on the Limits of Painting and Poetry. The parable of the Ring appears in this man's best known work, a play about religious tolerance featuring characters like Saladin and the titular philosopher modeled after Moses Mendelson. Name this author of Nathan the Wise.

One character in this novel has a fascination for a large wooden anchor that he nicknames Niobe; that character is Herbert Truczinsk, who has a tattoo of a hieroglyphic on his back that fascinates the protagonist. The protagonist of this work has conflicting accounts of his defense of a polish post office. Roswitha Raguna becomes the lover of the protagonist in the second part of this work, when he works at a circus. Sister Dorothea Köngetter is the focus of the third part of this work, when she is the love interest of the protagonist. The protagonist of this novel is a patient at a mental hospital whose scream can be used as a weapon; his name is Oskar Matzerath, and he refuses to grow. Name this novel which precedes Dog Years and Cat and Mouse in the Danzig Trilogy, a work by Gunther Grass.

After one character in this work remembers that another likes brandy, she remembers that he also loves "bergin," and a further development in that conversation reveals that the first character has an unpublished novel. Another character suggests that they dance to Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring, but the other characters decide that jazz would be a better choice. Another character remarks that certain women hiss like geese and South American whores, so one should beware of quicksand. A hysterical preganancy led to the marriage of two of the characters in this play, and those two characters suggest that they play games like Get the Guest and Humiliate the Host. The hosts' son had previously died by crashing his car into a tree, leading to the disappointment of his history professor father. Identify this play about Nick, George, Martha, and Honey, a work by Edward Albee.

Along with Paul Simon, this writer based a play on the murderer Salvador Agron entitled The Capeman. This author suggests that you "feat on your life" at the end of a poem in which you sit down to a mirror and greet yourself with elation, "Love After Love." In another play by this author, the prologue begins with Corporal Lestrade bringing in the protagonist, to whom a white woman sang and who is named Makak. In one of this man's poems, Kikuyu flies batten on a bloody pelt and the narrator asks "How can I turn" from the titular place "and live?" That poem is "A Far Cry from Africa," while a woman named Helen walks down the shore singing "Yesterday, all my troubles seemed so far away" in a modern adapation of an ancient epic set in this author's native St. Lucia. Name this author of Dream on Monkey Mountain and Omeros.

When one character in this novel is asked to define a horse, she replies by describing it as a hoofed quadruped. Mrs. Sparsit, resentful of being cast out of a comfortable position, spies on some characters in this novel. After a bank in this novel is robbed, one character suspects either Mrs. Pegler or Stephen Blackpool of doing the deed, the latter because he's been mistreated. One character in this novel realizes his mistake after his daughter returns to him instead of following through on her plans to elope with political aspirant James Harthouse, which is fortunate for him because she has been promised to marry manufacturer Josiah Bounderby. That same character believes that his children have been negatively influenced by daughter of a circus clown Sissy Jupe. Name this novel in which Thomas Gradgrind educates his children Louisa and Tom in "hard facts only," a novel by Charles Dickens.

The narrator of this noel has permanent stomach problems after he's forced to eat seven bananas after stealing a bunch of them from a politician. After leaving that job, he's forced to leave another after taking the fall for embezzling money from his employer in a rumshop. The protagonist of this novel has four children, including Anand, who is terrified after he becomes embroiled in a labor dispute which leads to the death of his dog. The protagonist of this novel moves to Port-of-Spain, where he achieves some success as a journalist. The protagonist of this novel is married in the Hanuman House to Shama, who is a member of the Tulsi clan from which the protagonist obtains the title object. Name this novel by V.S. Naipaul.

This novelist parodied positivist sociology in his scathing work Love and Pedagogy, while the identity of a public figure slowly becomes subsumed in his public face in this novelist's work Tulio Montalban. Some of his short stories were collected in the work The Mirror of Death, while in another work, he wrote about the Carlist siege of Bilbao,Peace in War. The title character of one of his novels slowly loses his faith but refuses to shake that of his parishioners, while in his most famous work, which he termed a nivola, Augusto is initially accepted but then rejected by Eugenia, who leaves to live with Mauricio. Name this man who wrote San Manuel Bueno, Martyr,and Mist, a member of the Generation of '98.

One character in this work describes an incident in which he stood on top of a church and yelled his defiance of God's will to the heavens. Ragnar Brovik is the son of one character in the employ of the protagonist of this play, and he's enamored of the title character's bookkeeper Kaia. One character in this work begs to have the opportunity to lay a wreath on the top spire of a building, while another character killed her children with tainted breast milk. The title character of this work had his house destroyed in a fire, which led him to have the opportunity to construct new homes on their ashes; those houses were inspired by the beautiful Hilda Wangel. Name this work in which Aline is married to the architect Halvard Solness, a play by Henrik Ibsen.

Some critics of this poem have focused on the role of the repetition of the words "and thought, and thought" in the second to last stanza. Other critics of this poem have noted its evocation of the Medici, although the subject of the poem "had never seen one." The title character of this poem dreams of "Thebes and Camelot" and "Priam's neighbors." Additionally, he "scorns the gold that he had sought," and is "would have sinned incessantly, could he have been one." In the final stanza, the title character of this poem "scratched his head and kept on thinking," but later "coughed, and called fate, and kept on drinking." identify this poem about a "child of scorn" who was "Born too late," a work by Edward Arlington Robinson.

One character in this novel notes that she hates studying history, because "The quarrels of popes and kings, with wars or pestilences in every page; the men all so good for nothing, and hardly any women at all — it is very tiresome," while that same character later notes that she cannot speak so well as to be unintelligible. The protagonist of this novel is forced to endure a public stagecoach journey on her own after she gets kicked out of the house in which she's staying, and she's frightened off by a man who enjoys hunting with dogs and saying "damn" a lot. Isabella at one point announces her intent to marry the protagonist's borther James. Although Jim Thorpe attempts to woo the protagonist of this novel, who enjoys reading Gothic novels, her real love interest is Henry Tilney. Identify this first of Jane Austen's novels to be published, written about the struggles of Catherine Morland for General Tilney's titular estate.

One of this man's poems notes that "some men like Jack and some like Jill; I'm glad I like them both, but still" and ends with him asking himself whether he's stray, or great. That poem, "Dubious," appeared before a poetry collection that was primarily meant for children, Beastly Tales. A novel by this man notably features an iguana named Arnold Schwarzenegger and the characters John and Liz, and is written entirely in verse; that novel, Golden Gate, appeared before another novel which features the violinst Michael and the pianist Julia, who fall in love and go to Vienna. This author of An Equal Music wrote a novel which features the families Khan, Chatterji, and Kapoor, who are attempting to find a match for the daughter of Rupa Mehra. Name this man who wrote the massive A Suitable Boy.

"The Movement" in this novel is opposed to the building of a railroad, and a character named Waiyaki is one of the leaders of that movement. The protagonist of this novel becomes disillusioned after a stay in prison when he finds that his wife has become pregnant in his absence. Lieutenant Koina returns to the central town in this novel for an uhuru celebration. That town, Thabai, also sees the flight of John Thompson, who was admired by Kuruja. Kihika reveals to one character in this novel that he had killed John Robson. One character in this novel is taken to the Rira camp; that man is Mugo, who will be murdered at the end of the novel. Mumbi is one of the most beautiful women in the area and is the wife of the carpenter protagonist of this novel, a man named Gikonyo. Name this novel about the Mau Mau Uprising in Kenya, an early work by Ngugi wa Thiong'o.

One character in this play runs into furniture after a walk on the beach because his father refuses to waste money on electricity. Near the end of this play, one character sneers "The Mad Scene: Enter Ophelia" as her mother drags her wedding dress downstairs. The maid Cathleen celebrates the distraction of the characters in this work by drinking all of their liquor. After one character notes that she hates it when her son becomes all gloomy and morbid, he replies by noting "It's pretty hard to have a dope fiend for a mother," referring to her morphine addition which she acquired after the birth of Edmund. A major argument in this play is about the illness of Edmund, who has tuberculosis, and is the son of James and Mary. Identify this play about the dissolution of the Tyrone family, the masterwork of Eugene O'Neill.

De Marsay urges Paul de Manerville not to get married in one part of this work, although he does so to Natalie Evangelista. Lucien de Rubempré and "Abbé Herrera" appear in one section of this work, which focuses on how to make up for the 60,000 francs that Lucien has gone into debt for. Those parts are The Marriage Contract andThe Harlots High and Low, Lucien had previously appeared in two previous parts of this work collected under the name Lost Illusions. A better-known part of this work sees the title character work with Valérie Marneffe to seduce a number of men; that part, usually grouped with Cousin Pons, is Cousin Bette. Also including a novel about the daughter of Felix who inherits his miserliness, name this work which includes Eugenie Grandet, a work by Honore de Balzac.

One of this man's newer works retells an ancient source which includes the story of a man who tried to hold back a Deluge for several years, known as Yu; that work is The Collection of Mountains and Seas. Two childhood friends reuinite, but soon part again, in this author's story "In the Park," while another story from the same collection portrays the reactions of a bus accident involving a cyclist, "The Accident." Those stories, which appeared after an absurdist play by this author entitled Signal Alarm, were collected in A Fishing Rod for my Grandfather. This man's best known novel features journeys down the Yangtze River and to the districts of Qiang, Miao and Yi, and during those journeys, the narration fragments from first person into second and third, mirroring the fragmentation of the narrator's identity on his quest for inner peace. Name this author of Soul Mountain, a Chinese novelist.
